column2: High in the Dragon Spine the last dragons of Caledor sleep, and each century fewer of them stir. The old secrets of the Dragon Princes are not wholly lost: with a decade of patient vigils in the smoking caves, gold for the keepers of the Dragon Shrine and a name the beasts will heed, a sleeping dragon might be woken and won as a steed.
I will climb to the caves at once.

Ten years of vigils in the heat of the caves have been rewarded. An ancient dragon has opened one burning eye, heard your name and judged you worthy. It will bear you into battle as its kind once bore Caledor Dragontamer himself. Let the world know of your glory!
I am a Dragon Prince in truth!
Word comes from Ulthuan that [From.GetBestName] has woken one of the sleeping dragons of Caledor and now rides it to war. Let the enemies of the Asur tremble...
I thought the dragons were all asleep!

The oldest of the vampires know how to stitch bone, sinew and the leathery wings of great bats into a monstrous steed, and to bind it with dark magic so that it will carry its master through the night and upon his prey. It will cost much of the necromantic power you have gathered, and years of work in the crypts.
I have better things to spend my power on.
After years of work in the crypts, the monster is finally ready. The shrieking abomination craves the blood of your enemies and will bear you wherever you wish.

A knight of the Blood Dragons as mighty as you deserves a steed to match. Somewhere beyond the storm clouds run the Nightmares, dark horses that no living rider can master. The quest to find one will keep you away from your court for some years.
Not now. Call off the quest.
There it is: a dark and twisted shape galloping through the clouds of a stormy night, eyes burning like coals. It bends to your will at last. It is time to ride home.

Since the dawn of Nehekhara, its kings have gone to war atop their chariots, and the Tomb Kings who woke from their deathly slumber lead their legions the same way. The artisans of the royal workshops can build you one worthy of your line in five years, plated in bronze and gold and drawn by skeletal steeds.
Your chariot is ready. Its armoured carriage shields you from harm, and from its high platform you can see the whole field and send your legions where they will strike hardest.

Great mammoths roam the frozen tundra of the north, where the tribes and the Ogres hunt them for meat, hides and bone. A few hunt them for war. Taking a bull alive and breaking it to the saddle is the work of years and costs many hunters, but a lord who rides one into battle can crush shield walls and batter down the gates of any stronghold.

After five hard years, the bull mammoth is broken. It towers over even the tallest of your warriors, a howdah of furs and iron on its back and the skulls of its tamers' foes on its tusks. Your enemies will hear it long before they see it.
Send hunters into the tundra to take a bull mammoth alive and break it for war. It takes five years.

The grooms come to you with their caps in their hands. Your [dying_mount.GetName] lay down in the straw last night and did not rise again. It carried you through mud and fire and the long roads of the Old World, and now the knackers wait at the stable door.
Bury it with honour. It earned that much.
The stablemaster leads out the foal you bred, no longer a foal at all. It has grown tall and sure-footed, it takes the bit without a fight, and it will bear a rider into battle now.
Saddle it. Let us see what it can do.

The beast market is all noise and dung and shouting. Horse-copers swear on their mothers' graves, drovers beat their charges through the crowd, and in the far pens something with too many teeth rattles its chains. What can be bought here depends on which breeding grounds lie near enough to your lands to send their stock. Where will you look first?
The pens of my own kind

Deep under the market the Skaven beast-masters keep their stock: squealing giant rats, Brood Horrors bred in Hell Pit, hulking Rat Ogres stitched together by Moulder flesh-crafters, and from the Skryre workshops, machines that roll and grind and spit green fire. Each of them for a price, each of them sworn to be the finest of the brood. Yes-yes.
A giant rat. Fast, cheap and hungry.
A Brood Horror. Hideous and mine.
A Rat Ogre to carry me into the fray.
A Doomflayer, all blades and warp-fire!

The Ogre beast-tamers of the Mountains of Mourn have brought their stock down from the high passes: shaggy Mournfangs that can gore a horse in half, and the rare Stonehorns, living avalanches of horn and rock-hard hide. They are fed on raw meat and they eat a great deal of it.

The skink handlers of the temple-cities keep the sacred beasts of Lustria as the Old Ones' plan commands: Ripperdactyls that nest on the ziggurats, Cold Ones that never tire, Carnosaurs whose roar shakes the jungle canopy, and the vast slow-walking Stegadons and Bastiladons. Which beast is fit for your role in the Great Plan?
A Ripperdactyl to take to the skies

Da beast-boyz have rounded up a whole lot of fings for a proppa warboss to ride. Squigs bouncin', wolves snarlin', boars stinkin' and somewhere in da back a spider da size of a hut. Pick one and krump it till it does wot it's told!
Hitch da boar to a chariot
§GTo ride a great spider is the highest honour for a servant of the Spider God§!
§GA squig can be made to carry you into battle, mostly in the right direction§!
§GA wolf rider shows the gobbos who's da fastest and da meanest§!
§GA boar shows da boyz who's tuff enough to lead 'em§!
§GGet dat gobbo engineer over 'ere, I want me chariot§!
Long lines of horses stand tethered under the awnings, from shaggy work-beasts to the great warhorses of the knightly orders. The horse-copers are already arguing over who saw you first.
These beasts have pulled carts and ploughs all their lives, and it shows. They will carry you, though no one will write ballads about it.
A palfrey fit for a noble
§GDray horses are mostly used as pack animals§!
§GRounceys are plain work horses. They give no advantage in battle, but they beat walking§!
§GPalfreys are gentle riding horses, much loved by nobles on parade§!
§GHobbies are light skirmishing horses from the misty isle of Albion, and often fertile§!
§GThe Estalian jennet is a small, light warhorse, and often fertile§!
Respectable horses that will not fail you, whether on the hunt or in the line of battle.
§GFirst bred for the hunt, coursers are now a common sight on the battlefield for their speed§!
§GDestriers are common warhorses, slower than coursers but stronger in close combat§!
§GThe heavy horses of Bretonnia are bred to carry a knight in full armour straight into the enemy line§!
§GBred in the Irrana Mountains of Estalia, these horses are sure-footed on rugged ground and strong in close combat§!
These are among the best mounts in the world, wondrous and terrible in equal measure on the battlefield. Their prices are as fearsome as they are.
Yoke my Cold One to a chariot
§GBred in the Land of Chill, these dark steeds are hardier and crueller than any horse of the Old World.[GetMountPrefixDesc]§!
§GCold Ones are savage reptiles driven by blood-lust to attack anything warm-blooded. Their slime numbs the rider's flesh, and their beast-masters sell them dear§!
§GYour Cold One will draw a war chariot§!
§GChargers are destriers bred for nothing but war. Followers of the Dark Gods get a beast already touched by Chaos§!
§GSteppe coursers are bred for speed and endurance on the open plains§!
§GThe Asur are famous for their swift cavalry, and their horses are made for skirmishing§!
§GArabyan horses are light and made for the deserts of Araby. They are often fair§!
§GUnlike the courser, this Arabyan horse is made for close combat. It is often fair§!
A war horse of the Chaos Wastes
§GThe Tong hordes raid Cathay and the Darklands on these swift, tireless horses. Lords within reach of Cathay pay less§!
§GThe mutated warhorses of the Wastes are more than a match for their southern cousins, and the warlords of the Dark Gods prize them. The Hung sell them cheaper§!
§GThe knights of Bretonnia are the finest heavy horse in the Old World, and these are their horses§!
§GDescended from horses brought from Ulthuan, these are bred for the attack and are often fair§!
Camels come from the deserts of the south, elephants from the Southlands and from far Ind, and mammoths only from the frozen north, where a few of the great beasts still roam.
§GArabyan camels cross the harshest deserts of Araby and fear nothing§!
§GCophic camels are slow from the rugged hills they come from, and mostly used to carry loads§!
§GSmaller than their Southlands cousins, the elephants of Ind are faster and still a terror in battle§!
§GThe great Southlands elephant is slow, and it crushes everything in its path§!
§GOnce the mammoths roamed the whole north of the world. Today only a few of these huge beasts survive in the frozen wastes, and only the Norscans and the Ogres sell them cheaply§!
Some beasts were never meant to carry a rider. That has never stopped the strong, the clever or the mad from trying, and the beast-dealers in this corner of the market charge accordingly.
§GThe Lamassu is a beast of Hashut with a bull's body, a mace-tipped tail and a great ugly head, as much daemon as animal§!
§GA Great Taurus is wreathed in fire and smoke. Its hide burns so hot that swords and axes soften and blunt on it§!
§GThe tigers of the southern jungles are deadly hunters that ambush their prey from the undergrowth§!
§GThe sorcerers of Araby bind spirits of the air into woven forms, and the flying carpet is the most famous of them§!
§GFew warbosses ever take to the skies on a wyvern, and fewer come back down the way they meant to§!
§GThese great bears live in the cold forests of the north and laugh at winter§!
§GThe winged horses of the Grey Mountains are prized by the knights of Bretonnia and the Empire alike§!
§GGriffons nest high in the mountains and are fierce and proud. Taming one is the work of years, which is why they cost so much§!
§GA light chariot drawn by dark steeds, quick enough to run down fleeing foes§!
§GThe dark pegasi of Naggaroth are bred for cruelty as much as for flight§!
§GThe beast-masters of Naggaroth sell a manticore only to a lord who can master it. It is a mount fit for a Dreadlord§!
A swift stag of Athel Loren
§GThe Asrai raise these great stags in the glades of Athel Loren. They are fast and well suited to skirmishing§!
§GA phoenix is a magical bird of Ulthuan, born of fire. If it lives long enough its fire may turn to frost§!
§GGreat Eagles are the largest birds of prey in the world, with a wingspan of over thirty feet and talons like swords§!

[Root.GetGovernorLetterGreeting]. [Root.GetChineseLetterBlessing].\n\nThe heavenly [From.Offmap.Ruler.GetLongChineseEmperorName] has graciously granted your wish. A fine horse from the imperial stables of Cathay is sent to you along the road west, with grooms to see it safely into your hands.
Since the §Y[offmap_cathay.GetFullName]§! suffers famine or plague, the horse arrives §Rweakened§!
This horse was bred for the Dragon Emperor's own guard: it is §GFair§! and §GSwift§!
None of the breeding grounds near your lands has a horse to spare for [FromFrom.GetBestName]. The commander will have to wait.

You mean to give [FromFrom.GetBestName] a horse for battle. All that remains is to choose which. Remember that if [FromFrom.GetSheHe] dies, gains land of [FromFrom.GetHerHis] own or is no longer your commander, the horse and its gear are lost.
A courser. You can never go wrong with speed.
A charger. I want [FromFrom.GetHerHim] in the thick of the fighting.
Perhaps now is not the time.
In the chaos of battle a stray arrow strikes your [current_mount.GetMountType] in the flank. It screams and stumbles, but it carries you on.
Word of the breeding grounds at [Root.GetName] has spread, and horse traders crowd its fairs. The locals grow fat on the trade, and so do the taxes they pay their liege.
The trade post at [Root.GetName] draws horse traders from far and wide to the breeding grounds. The locals grow fat on the trade, and so do the taxes they pay their liege.

A band of saddlers, harness-makers and farriers has come to [Root.GetName] seeking their fortune. They are skilled at the gear of riders and beasts, but they need money for tools and a workshop. A patron would share in their profits.

The physicians of the hospital in [Root.GetName] have done such good work that there are few sick left to treat, and they have begun to tend the beasts of the traders who pass through. The breeding grounds have never been healthier.
The horse traders of [Root.GetName] come to you with an offer. If you lend them some of your own land to graze their herds, they will give you a cut of their sales.
My land is not for their nags.
[Root.GetName] is famous for its breeding grounds, and the people love nothing more than a race. If you paid for a proper racecourse and purses for the winners, buyers would come from far and wide.
A life always on the move is hard on riders and horses alike, but it makes both of them tougher. Your [improved_horse.GetName] has grown used to running all day long across the plains.
For once there are no petitioners, no letters and no wars that need you. A few hours of peace. You could take your [random_mount.GetMountType] out, but where?
A slow ride around my lands
Thanks to the hard training and care of [stable_master.GetBestName], one of your mounts has grown into something better than it was.

Your stable master [stable_master.GetFirstName] comes to you with plans for training your [improved_mount.GetName]. Each comes with a special diet and care, and [stable_master.GetSheHe] swears that any of them will add years to the [improved_mount.GetMountType]'s life.
I want it to turn heads wherever it goes.
Let it crush all who stand in its way.
Let it outrun anything that chases it.

Shouting rises from the stable yard. Your stable master [stable_master.GetFirstName] and [stable_master_arguement_courtier.GetBestName] are at each other's throats over a broken saddle, a lame horse or an old insult, and half the court has come out to watch.
Enough. We are all friends here.

Your stable master [stable_master.GetFirstName] has worked tirelessly for years, and today [stable_master.GetSheHe] shows you the result: every beast in your stables is sleek, sound and in better health than ever. Surely such service deserves a reward.
A purse for my stable master!
Fire in the stables! A lamp kicked over in the straw, and the whole block went up. The grooms got the beasts out, but not before some of them were burned.
Your stable master [From.GetFirstName] is dead. The stables will miss [From.GetHerHim].

The grooms report that the feed is running low, and your [random_mount.GetName] is looking thin. The merchants offer everything from the best oats and fresh meat to sweepings off the granary floor. Good feed could bring the [random_mount.GetMountType] back to health.
Do not bother me with trifles. Anything will do.

I walk out among the herd to choose a warhorse. The grooms lead the best of the young stallions past me one by one, and I look them over with an eye trained since childhood: the depth of the chest, the set of the legs, the fire in the eye. One of them stands apart from the rest, strong and proud, and does not shy when I take its head.\n\nAs I swing up into the saddle I know I have chosen well. All that remains is to give it a name worthy of the steppe.

[Root.GetWarhorseName], my warhorse, has run its last gallop across the steppe and lain down for the long sleep. It carried me through raids and migrations, through snow and dust and the smoke of burning towns. It is time to say farewell to an old friend.

I have not been myself these last few weeks. Each morning I go out to the horse lines from habit, and each morning there is an empty place where [Root.GetWarhorseName] used to stand. It feels as if a piece of me is missing.
I must carry this burden alone.
I am lucky to have a [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] to comfort me.
I am lucky to have a friend to comfort me.

My ward [ward_cant_ride.GetFirstName] is nearly eight summers old and still cannot sit a horse properly. Children of the camp half [ward_cant_ride.GetHerHis] age gallop circles around [ward_cant_ride.GetHerHim] and laugh. It is a disgrace to my yurt.
This will not do! I shall teach [ward_cant_ride.GetHerHim] myself.

Riding from one of my camps to the next, we come to a river swollen with the spring melt, its rapids white and violent. The way around would cost us days, so we must cross. I watch from the bank as the party picks its way down into the churning water. [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetFirstName], my [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetHusbandWife], rides [Root.GetWarhorseName], my own warhorse.\n\nThen it happens. [Root.GetWarhorseName] loses its footing in the rapids, [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetFirstName] is thrown from the saddle, and the current takes them both. I have a heartbeat to act before they are swept away, and I cannot save them both...

I dragged [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetFirstName] out of the river by the hair. [Root.GetWarhorseName] is gone, carried off downstream, but my [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetHusbandWife] is safe. [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetSheHeCap] is shaking with cold and fright, and cannot stop thanking me for the rescue.

I dragged [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetFirstName] out of the river by the hair. Once on the bank, [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetSheHe] gets to [spouse_danger_nomad_river_crossing.GetHerHis] feet, dripping and shivering, and rounds on me: 'You fool! I can swim! How could you let a horse like that drown?'
I, too, now question my choice.

One of the warriors of my retinue has come to my tent with a plea. Sickness has gone through the warrior's herd: most of the family's mares are dead, there is no milk for the children, and the winter grazing is still months away.
You shall have six mares from my own herd.
A pity, but I cannot help you.

I was about to leave [Root.GetWarhorseName] at the watering hole when [From.GetFirstName]'s horse stretched out its neck and bit it, hard, on the shoulder. [Root.GetWarhorseName] screamed and reared, and [From.GetFirstName] only laughed.
There is a better watering spot over here...

A painter from the settled lands rode into my camp today with a pack-mule of brushes and pigments. The painter has painted the lords of many great houses, or so the boast goes, and would be honoured to paint whatever the [Root.GetTitle] wishes.
